channel.title: Genesis recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Genesis Fuel Pipe Leak May Increase Fire Risk
item.description: Fuel may leak from the connection point where the fuel pipe meets the fuel rail in these Genesis vehicles. A fuel leak in this location increases the risk of a fire. Genesis dealers will fix the problem by inspecting the connection and tightening it as needed, or by replacing the fuel pipe entirely if that turns out to be necessary for the vehicle.

item.title: Genesis and Hyundai Seat Belt Anchors May Detach
item.description: The seat belt anchors for the driver and front passenger may come loose from the vehicle. If an anchor detaches, the seat belt will not properly hold the occupant in place during a crash, which raises the risk of injury. Dealers will inspect the anchors and reinforce or replace them as needed, free of charge.

item.title: Genesis G80 and GV80 Instrument Display May Fail
item.description: A software error can cause the instrument panel display in front of the driver to fail. This display normally shows important information such as the speedometer and fuel gauge. If it stops working because of this software error, the driver may lose access to that information while driving.

item.title: Genesis G90 Radar May Cause Sudden Unintended Braking
item.description: The Highway Drive Assist system on these Genesis G90 vehicles uses a radar sensor at the corner of the vehicle to sense other cars. On some vehicles, that radar can mistakenly detect a vehicle that is not there. When it does, the car may brake suddenly and on its own while you are driving, without the driver intending it. Genesis will replace the front bumper beam to correct the problem.

item.title: Genesis GV60 windshield trim may come off vehicle
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Genesis GV60 electric vehicles. The stainless-steel strip of trim that sits along the top edge of the windshield may come loose and separate from the vehicle. A piece of trim that comes off can land on the road, where it becomes a hazard for other vehicles behind or around the car. Dealers will replace the windshield molding, and owners will be notified by mail.

item.title: Genesis G90 and GV60 Display Screen May Fail
item.description: Certain Genesis G90 and GV60 vehicles have a software error that can cause the instrument panel display to fail. That display normally shows drivers important information, such as the speedometer and warning lights. If it fails, that information is no longer shown while driving.

item.title: Genesis Instrument Panel Display May Fail
item.description: In certain Genesis G80, GV70, and GV80 vehicles, a software error can cause the instrument panel display to fail. This is the screen that normally shows things like the speedometer and warning lights, so a driver may not be able to see this information if it stops working. Dealers will inspect the instrument panel and update its software as needed to fix the problem, free of charge.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6, Genesis GV60 Charging Unit Failure
item.description: Certain Hyundai Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6, and Genesis GV60 vehicles have an Integrated Charging Control Unit that may become damaged. When this happens, the unit can stop charging the 12-volt battery. If the 12-volt battery is not being charged, the vehicle can lose drive power.

item.title: Genesis GV60, GV80 Backup Camera May Go Dark
item.description: In certain Genesis GV60 and GV80 vehicles, the rearview camera image may shut off while the vehicle is being driven in reverse. This means that the picture the camera normally shows on the display, which helps the driver see what is behind the vehicle, may disappear while the driver is backing up, leaving the driver without that view of what is behind the vehicle.

item.title: Hyundai, Genesis Fuel Pump May Cause Power Loss
item.description: Certain Hyundai and Genesis vehicles, including the Veloster N, Genesis G70, Elantra N, and Kona N, may have a fuel pump that fails. If the fuel pump fails, the vehicle can lose engine power while being driven. Some owners were sent an early letter warning them about this safety risk before the full notice with the repair information went out.

item.title: Genesis Fuel Pump Failure Can Cut Engine Power
item.description: The fuel pump that supplies fuel to the engine may fail. If it fails, the vehicle can lose the power that keeps it moving, even while you are driving. Losing drive power like this means the engine may stop providing the force needed to keep the vehicle moving forward on the road, which can happen at any time while driving these vehicles.

item.title: Genesis GV70 May Shift From Park to Neutral
item.description: Some Genesis GV70 vehicles may allow water to leak into the wiring harness for the transmission control system. If that happens, it can cause a short circuit inside the harness. This short circuit may cause the transmission to unexpectedly shift out of Park and into Neutral by itself, even though the driver has not touched the gear selector or done anything to cause the shift.

item.title: Hyundai and Genesis EV Charging Unit Can Fail
item.description: On these Hyundai and Genesis electric vehicles, the Integrated Charging Control Unit may become damaged and stop charging the 12-volt battery. This can result in a loss of drive power.

item.title: Genesis Turbo Oil Pipe May Leak, Risking Fire
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Genesis G70, G80, and G90 vehicles with a 3.3-liter turbocharged V6 engine. The left turbocharger oil feed pipe may deteriorate and leak oil. An oil leak near hot engine parts can increase the risk of a fire. Dealers will replace the left turbocharger oil feed pipe. This recall replaces an earlier recall, so vehicles already repaired under that recall will need the new repair completed.

item.title: Genesis G70, G80, G90 Starter Fire Risk
item.description: Water can get into a part of the starter system and cause an electrical short. This short can start a fire in the engine compartment, whether the vehicle is parked or being driven. Hyundai will install a new relay kit in the engine's electrical box to fix the problem.

item.title: Hyundai IONIQ 5, IONIQ 6, Genesis GV60 Driveshaft May Break
item.description: Certain 2023 Hyundai IONIQ 5, IONIQ 6, and Genesis GV60 vehicles have a rear inner driveshaft that may not have been heat-treated correctly during manufacturing. Because of this, the driveshaft can break when it is put under load, such as while accelerating. If the driveshaft breaks, the vehicle loses the power that turns the wheels, meaning it can no longer drive forward under its own power.

item.title: Genesis Fuel Pump Failure May Cut Power
item.description: On certain Genesis G80, GV70, and GV80 vehicles, the fuel pump may fail. If it does, the vehicle can lose drive power while being driven.

item.title: Genesis GV60 Passenger Seat Belt May Not Fasten
item.description: Certain 2023 Genesis GV60 vehicles have a problem with the automatic locking retractor for the front passenger-side seat belt. This retractor may prohibit the seat belt from fastening properly and may also prevent it from extending properly. Dealers will inspect the front passenger-side seat belt and replace it as necessary to correct the problem.

item.title: Genesis GV60 Rear Driveshafts May Fracture and Fail
item.description: Some all-wheel drive Genesis GV60 vehicles may have rear driveshafts that can fracture. If a driveshaft fractures, the vehicle can lose drive power.

item.title: Genesis G90 Seat Belt Pretensioners May Explode
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain 2023 Genesis G90 vehicles. In a crash, the seat belt pretensioners in the front and rear seats may explode when they deploy.

item.title: Genesis GV80, G80, GV70, GV60 seat belt part may explode
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Genesis GV80, G80, GV70 and GV60 vehicles. In a crash, the part that tightens the front seat belt can explode when it goes off. This can affect the driver side belt, the passenger side belt, or both. Dealers will secure these parts with a cap. This recall replaces and expands an earlier recall, so vehicles that were already repaired under that earlier one need the new repair as well.

item.title: Hyundai Sonata and Genesis G70 trunk latch can fail
item.description: The trunk latch on these cars can become damaged. When that happens, the trunk cannot be opened from the inside. Federal safety rules require a trunk release that works from within the trunk compartment, and these vehicles do not meet that requirement. Hyundai is recalling certain 2020 Sonata and Sonata Hybrid cars and 2019 Genesis G70 cars. Dealers will inspect the trunk latch and replace the latch base if it is needed, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Genesis and Hyundai Models Seat Belt Pretensioner Risk
item.description: On certain Genesis GV70, Genesis GV80, Hyundai Elantra, Elantra HEV, and Hyundai Venue vehicles, the front seat belt pretensioners on the driver's side, the passenger's side, or both may explode when they go off in a crash. If this happens, small metal pieces from the exploding pretensioner can be thrown into the vehicle's cabin and can strike the people riding inside, causing injury.

item.title: Genesis G80, GV80 Fuel Tube May Leak
item.description: Some Genesis G80 and GV80 vehicles equipped with certain turbo engines have a fuel tube that connects the high pressure fuel pump to the fuel rail. This tube may not seal properly. Because the seal may fail, fuel can leak out from where the tube connects to the fuel system.

item.title: Genesis G80 Brake Module May Catch Fire
item.description: The anti-lock brake module can malfunction and short-circuit. If that happens, it can start a fire in the engine area, whether the car is parked or being driven.

item.title: Genesis G70 Brake Module May Catch Fire
item.description: The anti-lock brake module can malfunction and short-circuit. If that happens, it can start a fire in the engine area, whether the car is parked or being driven.

item.title: Genesis G70 fuel pump defect may stall engine
item.description: Hyundai Motor America is recalling certain 2021 Genesis G70 vehicles with 2.0L GDI engines. A plastic burr left over from manufacturing may block the fuel pump's jet nozzle, which can leave the engine without enough fuel.

item.title: Genesis G80/G90 Turbo Oil Leak Fire Risk
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Genesis G80 and G90 vehicles equipped with 3.3-liter turbocharged engines. These vehicles have an oil supply pipe that feeds the turbocharger. On affected vehicles, the seal on this oil supply pipe may be loose rather than properly sealed. Because the seal is loose, oil from this pipe can leak out and land on the engine's exhaust manifold, rather than staying contained within the turbocharger's oil supply system.

item.title: Genesis G80 Airbag Sensor May Misread Passenger Seat
item.description: The passenger airbag system may wrongly detect that an adult is sitting in the front passenger seat, even when no one is there. Because of this misreading, if a child or infant is actually riding in that seat during a crash, the airbag may inflate instead of staying switched off, which is what should happen when a small child is in that seat. The system is not correctly recognizing who, or what, is actually in the seat.

item.title: Genesis G80, G90 Windshield May Detach
item.description: The windshield and rear window on these vehicles may have been installed with the wrong type of primer. This can weaken the bond that holds the glass to the vehicle frame. Because the incorrect primer was used, the strength of that bond may decrease over time, meaning the glass is not held in place as securely as it should be as the vehicle continues to be driven and used.
